subject: neuroscience
intro: Neuroscience leads to the study and care of the nervous system — neurologists and psychiatrists in the clinic, researchers probing circuits and memory, and the teachers who train them.

roles.title: Neurologists
roles.what: Diagnose, manage and treat disorders of the brain, spinal cord and peripheral nerves — stroke, epilepsy, movement disorders and neurodegenerative disease — with a primarily nonsurgical focus.
roles.where: Sections 2 to 4 — sensory pathways, motor systems and their disorders, hypothalamus and limbic system — with the brain-imaging-methods lesson mirror the neurology exam and workup.

roles.title: Psychiatrists
roles.what: Diagnose, treat and help prevent mental disorders, combining medical training with psychotherapy and medication management for conditions from depression and anxiety to psychosis.
roles.where: The neurotransmitter chapters of section 1, synaptic plasticity, and the neurotransmitter-and-drugs lesson connect the pharmacology of the synapse to the medications psychiatrists prescribe.

roles.title: Medical Scientists, Except Epidemiologists
roles.what: Conduct research into human disease and the improvement of health — laboratory and clinical investigation into how the brain and nervous system fail and how they can be treated.
roles.where: Genetics and neuronal disease (chapter 1.15), neurotransmitter and cell death, and the blood-brain-barrier chapters, with the brain-imaging-methods lesson, are the research questions lab scientists pursue.

roles.title: Neuropsychologists
roles.what: Apply theories and principles of neuropsychology to evaluate and diagnose disorders of higher cerebral functioning — memory, language, executive processing — often in research or medical settings.
roles.where: Section 4's learning-and-memory, language and executive-processing chapters, with the memory-circuits and consciousness lessons, are the assessment domains and theory this career tests.

roles.title: Health Specialties Teachers, Postsecondary
roles.what: Teach courses in the health specialties — medicine, therapy, laboratory technology — at universities and professional schools, often combining teaching with research.
roles.where: This textbook's medical-course structure — from resting and action potentials through motor systems to memory and higher cortical functions — is the progression a neuroscience educator reteaches and deepens.
